card.law_is_about: Modernising workplace biological-agent protections, including digital instruction and external exposure records.
card.they_want: Give stronger attention to combined exposure in occupational-medical assessment.
card.they_claim: A Liebers2020 endotoxin/organic-dust review is identified as JTEHB23(7):293–312.
card.the_problem: That interval lies inside a Cochard et al. atmospheric-particle review at pp293–318. A real Liebers2020 endotoxin review has different title/journal/pages; it is only a plausible alternative, not a demonstrated intended source.

correction: The publisher-deposited record for JTEHB23(7), pages293–318 identifies a2020 review by Cochard, Ledoux and Landkocz about atmospheric particles and epithelial transition, DOI10.1080/10937404.2020.1816238. The printed293–312 span falls inside this different article. Springer’s original2020 Liebers review concerns occupational endotoxin effects but is Archives of Toxicology94:3629–3644, DOI10.1007/s00204-020-02905-0. This is a possible bibliographic conflation, not a proved identification of the intended source.
effect: The cited journal location cannot verify the Liebers review that is named. Correcting the reference is needed to check the claimed supporting literature; it does not by itself resolve whether combined exposures warrant the requested assessment.
limits: No assertion that endotoxin or mixed exposures are harmless, that no Liebers review exists, or that the proposed occupational-medical clarification is wrong. No causal synergy estimate has been independently refuted. Metadata for the article occupying the stated journal pages was read; its full26-page text was not obtained (publisher access403). The real Liebers publisher abstract and bibliographic header were read; no full review of its clinical evidence is claimed.
materiality_explanation: Minor bibliographic verification error. Genuine relevant endotoxin literature exists, so the direction of any correction to the policy argument is unknown; no major material effect established.
context_and_alternatives: Both DGAUM pages read and physical2 visually checked. Section3 links the cited literature to combined biological/cofactor exposure and requests stronger comprehensive assessment in ABAS rules. An incorrect journal/page/title assembly or a miscopied reference is plausible. The existence of a genuine relevant Liebers2020 review limits policy implications while leaving the printed bibliographic mismatch clear.
